newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU and World Bank to strengthen partnership.
newsitem.headline: EU and World Bank to strengthen partnership.

text.p: The European Union and the World Bank agreed on Monday to bolster co-operation on a wide range of issues, including aid to former Yugoslavia and the emerging economies of Africa and central and eastern Europe.

After a meeting between World Bank president James Wolfensohn and European Commission President Jacques Santer, the two institutions said the rapidly increasing scale of private capital flows had made closer links necessary.
"This changing world environment brings new challenges to the European Union and to the World Bank Group," said Wolfensohn.
For former Yugoslavia, there was agreement to prepare for the next meeting of international donors, planned for the first quarter of 1997.
There was also a renewal of support for international high representative Carl Bildt in stressing the importance of sound economic policies in the region.
Together the World Bank and the Commission have prepared a three- to four-year, $5.1 billion reconstruction programme as a framework for donor support.
For Africa and eastern and central Europe, further help was pledged in easing the transition towards market-based economies.
